Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
957 AM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

Special Weather Statements for advection fog expired at 1300 UTC
for counties within the Beltway. A Marginal risk for severe 
thunderstorms was issued by SPC for Cecil County later today. A
Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for Anne Arundel County 
between 2100-0300 UTC; please refer to the Tides & Coastal 
Flood section for additional details. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Rain showers & perhaps a thunderstorm or two are possible 
  today, with the first snow for parts of the Alleghenies today 
  through Saturday.

- 2) Cooler temperatures and dry condtions expected into 
the middle of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... Rain showers & perhaps a thunderstorm or two
are possible today, with the first snow for parts of the Alleghenies
today through Saturday.

Showers and perhaps a few thunderstorms are expected today into
early this evening as low pressure tracks across the area. A 
low-end chance for a severe thunderstorm around northeast 
Maryland (mainly within Cecil County) exists for early this 
afternoon, with surface CAPE ranging up to 1000-1200 J/kg as a 
band of showers moves through the region. Dry PWATs and somewhat
elevated shear means that isolated hail or a short-lived weak 
tornado cannot be ruled out during this timeframe, although most
areas will see non-severe shower activity. 

A cold front will shift east of the area 
after 00Z tonight, with brisk NW winds developing and 
temperatures falling from the low 60s into the mid 50s by early 
evening and into the mid 40s by daybreak Fri. Across the higher 
elevations, temperatures will fall much more quickly into the 
upper 20s or low 30s by Fri morning. Off and on snow showers are
anticipated across the mountains late tonight into Sunday 
morning. Despite plenty of cold air to support snow, snow 
accumulations have continued to trend downward as a result of 
unfavorable low-level trajectories. This still looks like a 
light snow event of 1 to 2 inches falling over a 24-hr period, 
which does not meet the criteria for a Winter Weather Advisory. 
Elsewhere, light rainfall accumulations of a tenth to two tenths
of an inch are expected, mainly this afternoon. 

Continued brisk conditions are expected into Monday with plenty
of stratocumulus clouds during the daytime hours. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler temperatures and dry condtions expected into 
the middle of next week.

Longwave troughing will remain over the east coast through early 
next week, although heights will start rising Monday as the 
amplified upper level pattern slowly progresses eastward. 
Likewise, low level trajectories will gradually become less 
favorable for upslope snow showers Sunday. Winds should be much 
less noticeable by Monday and Tuesday as the surface high 
finally reaches the Mid Atlantic, although temperatures remain 
below normal. Given the lighter winds, the subsequent nights 
could turn out colder in many areas, with widespread near or 
below freezing temperatures outside of the urban centers and 
tidal shoreline.

Further upper level amplification will likely happen toward mid 
week. While a trough or low could develop toward the southeast 
coast, it appears that ridging will dominate the Mid Atlantic. This 
should start a warming trend beginning Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...

Patchy to dense advection fog has lifted for the most part as of
15Z this morning, and VSBYs should continue to improve through
the morning save for periodic rain showers/thunderstorms that 
move through. Scattered to numerous light showers are expected 
today into early this evening, mainly in the 18Z Thu - 00Z Fri 
time frame. No flight restrictions are currently expected, but 
cigs will be BKN-OVC around 4kft. Winds will shift to the NW 
after 00Z Fri and pick up speed with gusts to 20 kt. Winds 
strengthen further Fri and Sat with better mixing with gusts to 
around 30 kt expected. BKN- OVC stratocumulus deck is expected 
Fri-Sun during the day.

Northwest winds may gust up to 25 kt Sunday, then become lighter 
Monday. Otherwise VFR conditions are expected both days.

&&

.MARINE...

Winds will strengthen this evening after frontal passage with
frequent gusts to 20 kt expected. Winds strengthen further Fri 
into Sat with gusts to 30 kt expected. 

Small Craft Advisory conditions will continue in northwest flow 
through probably Monday. Winds will start decreasing Sunday 
night and Monday as high pressure nears, although marginal 
advisory conditions may persist along the bay for a time.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Action Stages are likely tonight before winds shift to 
northwest behind a cold front this evening. Annapolis is now
forecast to reach minor coastal flooding with the high tide this
evening. A Coastal Flood Advisory has thus been issued for Anne
Arundel County until 0300 UTC. A strong frontal passage will 
bring a prolonged period of blowout tides Friday and through 
early next week.

&&

     MDZ014.
